title: EmSAT English
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public EmSAT English syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A notice explains that the town library will stay open until 9 p.m. on weekdays and until 5 p.m. on Saturdays, but will close entirely on Sundays. According to the notice, when is the library closed all day?
items.explanation: The notice says the library closes entirely on Sundays while weekdays run until 9 p.m. and Saturdays until 5 p.m., so only Sunday is a full closure.

items.stem: A passage describes how a coastal town built a sea wall, restored sand dunes, and planted mangroves, and reports that storm damage fell by half over five years. What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A sea wall alone is the cheapest option.
Combining several defences reduced storm damage.
Mangroves grow faster than sand dunes.
items.explanation: The passage lists three measures working together and reports a large fall in storm damage, so the main idea is that combined defences cut damage.

items.stem: A text notes that although the new train line opened only last month, ticket sales already exceed the operator's first-year target. What can be inferred from this?
options: The line will close next year.
Tickets were given away for free.
The line is more popular than the operator expected.
The operator set no targets at all.
items.explanation: Sales beating a first-year target within a month shows demand is higher than the operator had forecast, so the line is more popular than expected.

items.stem: A guide states that the museum's Egyptian gallery is on the first floor, the dinosaur gallery is on the ground floor, and the cafe is in the basement. On which floor is the Egyptian gallery?
items.explanation: The guide places the Egyptian gallery on the first floor, while the dinosaur gallery is on the ground floor and the cafe is in the basement.

items.stem: A report says the evidence for the claim is scant, resting on a single small study. As used in the report, the word scant most nearly means which of the following?
items.explanation: The report says the evidence rests on one small study, so scant means insufficient rather than abundant, recent or convincing.

items.stem: An article lists the ingredients on a snack packet, explains what each additive does, and warns that two of them can cause reactions in some people. What is the writer's main purpose?
options: To sell the snack to readers
To inform readers about the additives in the snack
To describe the factory where it is made
items.explanation: The article explains what the additives do and warns of possible reactions, so its purpose is to inform readers about those ingredients.

items.stem: A weather report states that heavy rain is expected on Tuesday, clear skies on Wednesday, and strong winds on Thursday. On which day are strong winds expected?
items.explanation: The report links strong winds to Thursday, while Tuesday brings heavy rain and Wednesday is described as clear.

items.stem: A manager's email says the team met every deadline this quarter but adds that two clients have not yet renewed their contracts. What does the email suggest?
options: All of the clients have renewed already.
Good performance alone does not guarantee renewals.
items.explanation: Meeting deadlines yet facing unrenewed contracts suggests that strong performance does not automatically secure client renewals.

items.stem: A passage explains that bees, butterflies and some birds all pollinate plants, and that removing any one of them can reduce fruit harvests. What is the passage mainly about?
options: Several different animals matter for pollination.
Bees are the only true pollinators.
items.explanation: The passage names several pollinators and says losing any one reduces harvests, so its main point is that many animals matter for pollination.

items.stem: A passage states that the river begins in the mountains, flows through the capital, and empties into the sea. According to the passage, the river flows through which place?
items.explanation: The passage says the river flows through the capital after leaving the mountains and before reaching the sea.

items.stem: A reviewer writes that the film's scenery is breathtaking but its plot is so thin that the reviewer checked the time twice. What is the reviewer's overall view?
items.explanation: Praising the scenery while criticising the thin plot gives a mixed view in which the visuals are praised but the story is not.

items.stem: A study finds that students who walked to school arrived more alert than those who were driven, even when both groups slept the same number of hours. What does this suggest?
options: Sleep has no effect on alertness at all.
items.explanation: With sleep held constant, the alertness advantage of the walkers points to morning exercise rather than sleep as the cause.

items.stem: A passage describes how a city converted empty roofs into gardens that cool buildings, absorb rain and provide vegetables. What is the passage mainly about?
options: The benefits of urban rooftop gardens
The cost of building new parks
The history of a single family
items.explanation: The passage lists cooling, rain absorption and food as advantages of rooftop gardens, so those benefits are its main subject.

items.stem: A leaflet says the swimming pool is open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. on weekdays and from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. at weekends. On Saturday, at what time does the pool close?
items.explanation: The leaflet gives weekend hours of 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., so on Saturday the pool closes at 6 p.m. rather than 10 p.m.

items.stem: A text says the old bridge is dilapidated and that engineers fear it could fall. As used here, the word dilapidated means which of the following?
items.explanation: The engineers fear the bridge could fall, so dilapidated means in a state of disrepair rather than safe, new or admired.

items.stem: A leaflet explains how to recycle glass, paper and metal, and it lists the nearest collection points for each material. What is the leaflet's purpose?
options: To tell readers how and where to recycle
items.explanation: The leaflet explains recycling methods and names collection points, so it aims to tell readers how and where to recycle each material.

items.stem: A report says a factory installed new filters and that nearby air quality readings have improved every month since. What can be inferred from the report?
options: The new filters may be improving air quality.
The factory has now closed down.
The air quality was always perfect.
items.explanation: Air quality improving each month after the filters were fitted suggests the filters are helping, though the report does not prove causation.

items.stem: A passage explains that some desert plants store water in thick leaves, others have deep roots, and others shed their leaves in dry months. What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why deserts become cold at night
Ways desert plants survive with little water
How to grow roses in a garden
The speed at which sandstorms travel
items.explanation: Each example describes a different survival method for dry conditions, so the passage is about how desert plants cope with little water.

items.stem: A timetable shows that the morning ferry leaves at 7.30, the afternoon ferry at 1.15 and the evening ferry at 6.45. At what time does the afternoon ferry leave?
items.explanation: The timetable labels the 1.15 departure as the afternoon ferry, distinct from the 7.30 morning and 6.45 evening services.

items.stem: A columnist argues that banning cars from the city centre was bold, necessary and long overdue. What is the columnist's attitude towards the ban?
items.explanation: Calling the ban bold, necessary and long overdue is clear approval, so the columnist strongly supports the measure.

items.stem: Choose the sentence that is grammatically correct in standard written English.
options: She has lived in Abu Dhabi since 2015.
She has lived in Abu Dhabi since 2015 ago.
She is living in Abu Dhabi since 2015.
She lives in Abu Dhabi since 2015.
items.explanation: The present perfect 'has lived' pairs with 'since' plus a point in time, so the other options mix tenses that do not fit the time phrase.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct relative pronoun. The report, ______ was published yesterday, contains several errors.
items.explanation: 'Which' is the correct relative pronoun for a thing, the report; 'who' is used for people and 'what' cannot introduce this kind of clause.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct verb form in this conditional sentence. If I ______ more time, I would learn another language.
items.explanation: This is a second conditional about an unreal present, so the if-clause takes the past simple 'had' with 'would' in the main clause.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement.
options: The list of names were left on the desk.
The list of names are left on the desk.
The list of names have left on the desk.
The list of names was left on the desk.
items.explanation: The subject is 'list', which is singular, so the verb must be 'was'; the phrase 'of names' does not change the number of the subject.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Select the correct preposition to complete the sentence. The train arrived ______ time despite the storm.
items.explanation: The fixed expression is 'on time', meaning punctually, so 'on' is the only correct preposition in this sentence.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct pronoun to complete the sentence. Between you and ______, I think the plan will fail.
items.explanation: After the preposition 'between' an object pronoun is needed, and 'me' is the object form, while 'I' is a subject pronoun.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct article. She is ______ honest woman.
items.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound because the h is silent, so the indefinite article is 'an', not 'a'.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct comparative form. This exam is ______ than the last one.
items.explanation: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y form the comparative with -ier, so 'easier' is correct rather than 'more easy'.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct modal verb to complete the sentence. You ______ wear a seatbelt because it is the law.
items.explanation: The law makes the action obligatory, which the modal 'must' expresses, while the other options suggest possibility or preference.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct passive form to complete the sentence. The bridge ______ built in 1890.
items.explanation: The singular subject 'bridge' takes the past passive 'was built', while 'were' is plural and the other options do not form a correct passive.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition. He apologised ______ arriving late.
items.explanation: The verb 'apologise' is followed by 'for' plus a gerund, so 'for arriving' is the correct pattern in this sentence.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct tense to complete the sentence. By the time we arrived, the film ______.
items.explanation: The past perfect 'had started' marks the earlier of two past events, which fits the film starting before our arrival.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the sentence that uses a gerund correctly as the subject.
items.explanation: A gerund, which is the -ing form used as a noun, can be the subject, so 'Swimming is good exercise' is correct.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct verb. Neither the teacher nor the students ______ ready.
items.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students', which is plural, so 'were' is the correct form.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct quantifier. There is ______ milk left, so we need to buy more.
items.explanation: 'Milk' is uncountable, so it takes 'little'; 'few', 'many' and 'several' are used with countable nouns instead.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct adverb form to complete the sentence. She speaks English ______.
items.explanation: The verb 'speaks' is modified by an adverb, so 'fluently' is correct rather than the adjective 'fluent' or a noun form.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Select the sentence that is correctly punctuated.
options: We bought apples, bananas, and oranges.
We bought apples bananas and oranges.
We bought, apples bananas, and oranges.
We bought apples bananas, and oranges
items.explanation: Items in a list are separated by commas, so a comma after 'apples' and after 'bananas' is required for correct punctuation.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Complete the first conditional sentence. If it rains tomorrow, we ______ the match.
items.explanation: The first conditional pairs a present-tense if-clause with 'will' in the main clause, so 'will cancel' is the correct form.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence. The team played ______ than their rivals.
items.explanation: The comparative adverb 'better' compares the team's play with the rivals', while 'good' and 'well' are not comparative forms.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence. I look forward to ______ from you.
items.explanation: 'Look forward to' takes a gerund, so 'hearing' is correct rather than the bare infinitive or a past form.
items.reference: EmSAT English Syllabus - Language and Grammar

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. The scientist's findings were ______ by three independent laboratories.
items.explanation: 'Confirmed' means verified, which fits laboratories checking and supporting the findings, while the other words mean unrelated things.

items.stem: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word 'rapid'.
items.explanation: 'Rapid' means fast or quick, so 'quick' is the closest synonym, whereas 'slow' is its opposite in meaning.

items.stem: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to the word 'expand'.
items.explanation: 'Expand' means to grow larger, so its opposite is 'shrink', while 'grow', 'stretch' and 'widen' share its meaning.

items.stem: Choose the verb that correctly completes the collocation to ______ a decision.
items.explanation: English collocates 'decision' with 'make', as in 'to make a decision', while 'do' and 'take' do not form this fixed phrase.

items.stem: Choose the word that best fits the sentence. The ancient temple is a ______ of great historical importance.
items.explanation: A 'monument' is a structure of historical importance, which fits the sentence, while the other options are unrelated words.

items.stem: As used in the sentence 'The manager was reluctant to approve the plan', the word reluctant means which of the following?
items.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling or hesitant, so it contrasts with 'eager', 'certain' and 'delighted', which suggest enthusiasm or confidence.

items.stem: The prefix 'mis-' in the word 'misunderstand' carries which of the following meanings?
items.explanation: 'Mis-' means wrongly or badly, so 'misunderstand' means to understand wrongly, while other prefixes carry the other meanings.

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. Regular exercise can ______ the risk of heart disease.
items.explanation: 'Reduce' means to lower, which fits lowering the risk of disease, while the other words mean to make or bring something about.

items.stem: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word 'abundant'.
items.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large amounts, so 'plentiful' is the closest synonym, whereas 'scarce' is its opposite.

items.stem: Choose the word that best fits the sentence. The evidence was ______, so the court dismissed the case.
items.explanation: A court dismisses a case when the evidence is too weak, so 'insufficient' fits, while the other words are unrelated to proof.

items.stem: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to the word 'ancient'.
items.explanation: 'Ancient' means very old, so its opposite is 'modern', while 'old', 'historic' and 'aged' all share the idea of being old.

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. She gave a ______ explanation that everyone could follow.
items.explanation: 'Clear' means easy to understand, which fits an explanation everyone could follow, while the other options mean the opposite.

items.stem: The suffix '-less' in the word 'careless' carries which of the following meanings?
items.explanation: '-less' means without, so 'careless' means without care, whereas the suffix '-ful' would mean full of something.

items.stem: Choose the word that best fits the sentence. The two countries signed a ______ to end the dispute.
items.explanation: A 'treaty' is a formal agreement between countries, which fits ending a dispute, while the other words are unrelated in meaning.

items.stem: Choose the verb that correctly completes the collocation to ______ a mistake.
items.explanation: English collocates 'mistake' with 'make', as in 'to make a mistake', while 'do', 'build' and 'create' do not form this idiom.

items.stem: In the sentence 'The instructions were ambiguous', the word ambiguous means which of the following?
options: open to more than one meaning
items.explanation: 'Ambiguous' describes something with more than one possible meaning, so the instructions were unclear rather than simple or accurate.

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. The medicine had a ______ effect and the fever dropped within an hour.
items.explanation: A drop in fever shows a good result, so 'beneficial' fits, while 'harmful' and 'negative' contradict the improvement described.

items.stem: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word 'genuine'.
items.explanation: 'Genuine' means real or authentic, so 'authentic' is the closest synonym, while 'imitation' carries the opposite meaning.

items.stem: Choose the word that best fits the sentence. The company had to ______ its workforce because sales had fallen sharply.
items.explanation: Falling sales lead firms to cut staff numbers, so 'reduce' fits, while 'expand' and 'increase' would mean the opposite.

items.stem: In the phrase 'a vivid description', the word vivid means which of the following?
options: producing clear, strong images in the mind
items.explanation: 'Vivid' describes something that creates clear, powerful images, so a vivid description is lively and detailed rather than dull.
